objective: By the end of this lesson you can set up VOR, DME and GPS equipment for a hold, teach holding speeds, fix recognition, entry choice, timing, wind correction, DME holds and ATC reports in simple steps, demonstrate a hold while explaining it, use the MFD to monitor it, and name, explain and fix a learner's holding errors.
why: Holding protected airspace was built around the FAA's three entries, and a different entry flown with too much speed can take an airplane outside it [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3]]. ATC watches holding airspace on radar only when it can, and that never relieves the pilot of staying in the hold [[33:392|AIM 5-3-8l]], so the learner's own setup, timing and wind correction are what keep the airplane safe. The CFII PTS makes this Task part of every CFII practical test unless you already hold an instrument instructor rating in another category [[FAA-S-8081-9E:18|PTS Additional Rating Table]] [[FAA-S-8081-9E:38|PTS Area VII NOTE]], and the evaluator will play your student.

warmup: Think first: your instrument learner flies a neat parallel entry. After that, every inbound leg takes about 1 minute 30 seconds and rolls out right of course. She tells you her outbound heading is simply her inbound heading plus 180. What two errors do you see, and which do you fix first?

key_terms.def: A predetermined maneuver that keeps an aircraft within a specified airspace while it waits for further clearance from ATC [[34:357|P/CG H-2]].
A fix the pilot can identify by NAVAIDs or by visual reference, used as the reference point for holding [[34:357|P/CG H-2]].
Standard: right turns. Nonstandard: left turns [[33:385|AIM 5-3-8j1]].
The side of the holding course where the racetrack is flown; the other side is the nonholding side [[33:385|AIM FIG 5-3-3]].

The time a pilot can expect clearance beyond a clearance limit [[34:342|P/CG E-3]]; with lost radios in IFR conditions it is when to leave the clearance limit, or to begin the approach if the limit is a fix where an approach begins [[60:483|14 CFR 91.185(c)(3)]].
200 KIAS from the MHA to 6,000 ft, 230 KIAS from 6,001 to 14,000 ft and 265 KIAS above, unless charted lower [[33:385|AIM 5-3-8j2(a)]].
The lowest altitude for a holding pattern that gives signal coverage, communications and obstacle clearance [[34:379|P/CG M-4]].
The line through the fix on the holding side that the entry sectors are drawn from, in left-turn and right-turn holds alike [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3(e)]].
The point on the outbound leg even with the fix. Outbound timing starts over or abeam the fix, whichever is later [[33:385|AIM FIG 5-3-3]] [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4(b)]].
With the VOR set to the reciprocal of the course flown, the CDI senses backwards, so the pilot turns away from the needle [[23:257|IFH 9-14]].
DME distance measured in a straight line to the station, not along the ground [[33:72|AIM 1-1-7b]]; negligible at 1 NM or more per 1,000 ft above the facility [[23:262|IFH 9-19]].
The GPS distance readout that marks the end of the outbound leg on a GPS hold, in place of DME [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j5]].

chunks.title: Setting up VOR, HSI, DME and ADF for the hold

body.p: A hold is a predetermined maneuver that keeps the aircraft within a specified airspace while it waits for further clearance, anchored on a fix the pilot can identify by NAVAIDs or visual reference [[34:357|P/CG H-2]]. So the hold is only as good as the equipment that finds the fix. The Instrument lesson IR.III.B covers the pilot's side of holding; this lesson adds how you teach it and how you fix a learner's errors.

**Setting of aircraft navigation equipment.** When a delay is anticipated, ATC usually issues the holding clearance at least 5 minutes before the fix [[29:111|IPH 2-51]]. That is the learner's setup window, so teach the setup as a fixed routine done early, not at the fix.

head: Equipment
Set it this way
Why
rows: VOR receiver
Tune it, then identify it by Morse code or by the recorded voice ID that ends in "VOR"

The only positive way to identify a VOR [[33:68|AIM 1-1-3c]]; listen to the identifier before relying on the instrument [[23:254|IFH 9-11]]. A unit that decodes and displays the ID needs no listening [[33:69|AIM 1-1-3c]]
OBS on a plain CDI
The inbound course to the fix

Flying the reciprocal of the selected course gives reverse sensing: turn away from the needle [[23:257|IFH 9-14]]. On the outbound leg the learner is flying the reciprocal, so warn her before she gets there
HSI course pointer
The inbound course
The HSI shows the airplane against the course as if seen from above [[23:118|IFH 5-23]] and lowers workload in tasks such as a holding pattern entry [[23:254|IFH 9-11]]
Heading bug
The next heading: the entry heading, then the outbound heading with its wind correction
Bugs remind the pilot of assigned headings and courses, a basic error-reduction tool [[25:85|AIH 3-34]]
DME
Channeled to the holding facility, with its ID checked

The DME ID is a higher tone heard once for every three or four VOR IDs; one ID about every 30 seconds means the DME works but the VOR does not. A DME HOLD function keeps it on the station it was tuned to before HOLD was set [[23:260|IFH 9-17]]
ADF (NDB hold)
Tuned and identified, ID monitored; heading indicator matched to the compass

The ADF has no warning flag, so monitor the NDB ID continuously [[33:68|AIM 1-1-2d]]. A heading indicator that disagrees with the compass, and improper tuning and station identification, are listed ADF errors [[23:251|IFH 9-8]]
Clock or timer
Ready to note the time at the fix and to start again over or abeam it
The entry time reported is the first arrival over the fix [[23:303|IFH 10-12]]; outbound timing starts over or abeam the fix, whichever is later [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4(b)]]

body.p: Two cautions for any VOR: if a NOTAM calls the transmitter unusable, disregard its indications however good they look [[33:68|AIM 1-1-1b]]. And expect some roughness: at a few stations, usually in mountainous terrain, a brief needle oscillation like the one seen approaching the station, so use the TO/FROM indicator for positive station passage [[33:69|AIM 1-1-3e2]].

callout.text: Application: have the learner say the setup aloud in the same order every time, for example: tune, identify, set the course, set the bug, ready the clock, plan the report. Standard routines for routine tasks are a proven way to reduce error [[25:85|AIH 3-34]].

check.q: Your learner tunes the holding VOR and sets the OBS, but skips the ident because the needle came alive. What do you tell her?
check.a: The only positive identification of a VOR is its Morse code or recorded voice ID [[33:68|AIM 1-1-3c]], and careless tuning and identification is the first VOR error the IFH lists [[23:257|IFH 9-14]]. A live needle can come from the wrong station.

chunks.title: Setting up a GPS or RNAV hold

body.p: A suitable RNAV system, such as IFR-approved GPS, may stand in for a VOR, DME, TACAN or NDB that is out of service, or for an ADF or DME that is not installed or not working [[33:116|AIM 1-2-3a1]], and may be used to hold over a VOR, TACAN, NDB, compass locator or DME fix [[33:117|AIM 1-2-3c]]. A pilot substituting for an out-of-service NAVAID may need to tell ATC [[33:117|AIM 1-2-3a NOTE]].

RNAV holding works differently from one system to the next, and pilots are expected to know the capabilities and limits of their own [[33:388|AIM 5-3-8j7]]. All holds, RNAV ones included, are still built on the conventional NAVAID holding criteria [[33:388|AIM 5-3-8j7(a)]]. What to check with the learner:

bullets: **Database holds.** Several holds with different turns and legs can exist at one fix, but many systems store only one. The pilot must confirm turn direction, speed limit, timing and distance match the hold assigned [[33:390|AIM 5-3-8j7(c)(1)]].
**Left turns.** Some systems store every hold as standard and need pilot action for left turns [[33:390|AIM 5-3-8j7(c)]].
**Uncharted holds.** The pilot programs the assigned course, turn direction, speed limit, leg length or leg time [[33:390|AIM 5-3-8j7(c)(2)]].
**Late changes.** Changes made close to the fix may not apply until the next circuit [[33:390|AIM 5-3-8j7(c)(3)]].

**Limits taken from the current altitude.** Loading a hold above 14,000 ft for a hold below it can give 1½-minute timing, and a pilot-modified leg time usually stays modified after a descent [[33:389|AIM 5-3-8j7(a)(5)]] [[33:390|AIM 5-3-8j7(a)(5)]].

**Sequencing.** Some receivers need the pilot to stop waypoint sequencing for a hold and restart it after [[23:273|IFH 9-30]]. For a GPS hold over an NDB the IFH steps are: check integrity, select the facility from the database, select a nonsequencing mode such as HOLD or OBS with the course, and hold per the POH/AFM [[23:271|IFH 9-28]].

body.p: How to teach the box: the IFH lists entering, flying and exiting holds among the receiver tasks to practice [[23:275|IFH 9-32]], and advises learning a receiver in VFR before using it under IFR [[23:271|IFH 9-28]]. Tie every button press to a check of what it did: anticipate, act, verify [[30:51|RMH 7-2]].

callout.text: Many systems choose the entry from ground track, not heading, so a strong crosswind can give an entry the learner did not expect [[33:388|AIM 5-3-8j7(a)(1)]]. Brief it before the first windy GPS hold.

check.q: ATC assigns left turns at a fix where your learner's GPS already has a stored hold. She presses the hold key and moves on. What do you ask her to do?
check.a: Check that the stored hold matches the clearance in turn direction, speed limit, timing and distance; that is the pilot's job [[33:390|AIM 5-3-8j7(c)(1)]]. Some systems store holds as standard and need pilot action for left turns [[33:390|AIM 5-3-8j7(c)]].

chunks.title: Holding airspeed for the airplane and the altitude

body.p: **Requirement for establishing the appropriate holding airspeed for the aircraft and altitude.** The size of a hold is directly proportional to speed, so maximum holding speeds limit the airspace ATC must protect [[29:112|IPH 2-52]].

head: Altitude (MSL)
Maximum holding airspeed
rows: MHA to 6,000 ft
14,001 ft and above

bullets: **Charted limits.** Some holds from 6,001 to 14,000 ft are limited to 210 KIAS, shown by an icon; a speed in parentheses inside the pattern, such as (175), should be met before first crossing the fix [[33:385|AIM 5-3-8j2(b)]]. 175 KIAS holds are generally on approaches for category A and B aircraft [[23:302|IFH 10-11]].

**The low end.** Fixed-wing airplanes should hold at 90 KIAS or faster to limit wind drift. With RNAV guidance, hold at the lowest practical airspeed consistent with the airplane's recommended holding speed [[33:390|AIM 5-3-8j8(a)(1)]].

**When to slow.** With advance notice, be at or below the maximum at least 3 minutes before the fix; without notice, slow as soon as practical [[33:390|AIM 5-3-8j8(a)]]. Within 3 minutes of a clearance limit with no clearance beyond it, start slowing to cross the fix at or below the maximum [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8d]]. The purpose is to avoid overshooting the holding airspace, especially where holds are close together [[23:302|IFH 10-11]].
**Can't comply.** If turbulence or icing needs more speed, tell ATC at once and ask for another clearance; without radar, tell ATC you cannot accept the hold [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(a)(2)]].

body.p: The sources give the limits; the speed and power for your trainer come from its POH. Slowing on the way to the fix can also shorten or avoid the hold [[29:112|IPH 2-52]]. A slower airplane needs less bank for a standard-rate turn, which matters when the learner slows for holding: a rule of thumb is airspeed divided by ten plus 7, so 90 knots needs about 16° [[23:88|IFH 4-11]].

callout.text: Build the speed habit before the first real hold with the IFH racetrack pattern: time 3 minutes of level flight while slowing to the airplane's holding speed, turn 180° at standard rate, fly 1 minute, turn again, and adjust the outbound leg for a 1-minute inbound leg [[23:191|IFH 7-30]].

check.q: Your multiengine learner, holding at 9,000 ft, says he may fly 230 knots anywhere below 14,000 ft. The chart shows (175) inside the racetrack. What do you teach?
check.a: A speed in parentheses is the maximum for that hold; be at or below it before first crossing the fix to stay in protected airspace [[33:385|AIM 5-3-8j2(b)]]. 230 KIAS is only the general limit from 6,001 to 14,000 ft [[33:385|AIM 5-3-8j2(a)]].

chunks.title: Arriving at the fix: recognize it, then turn

body.p: **Recognition of arrival at the holding fix and the prompt initiation of entry into the holding pattern.** The protected airspace assumes the airplane flies over the fix on entry [[33:388|AIM 5-3-8j7(a)(2)]], so every second of a late turn uses up room. Before the fix, the learner should know what passage will look like on the box being used.

head: Fix
What passage looks like
Instructor note
rows: VOR
The first complete reversal of the TO/FROM indicator: begin the turn outbound then [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8g]]
Close to the station the CDI moves fast or swings from side to side in the zone of confusion [[23:257|IFH 9-14]]; use the TO/FROM for positive passage [[33:69|AIM 1-1-3e]]
Intersection
The crossing radial from a second NAVAID centers
One NAVAID gives a radial; a second one is needed to fix the exact point on it [[23:257|IFH 9-14]]. Preset the second receiver early
DME fix
The DME reads the fix distance while on the holding course [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j5]]
With GPS, the pilot is over the fix when the distance from the DME facility waypoint equals the charted DME value and the airplane is on the right course [[23:270|IFH 9-27]]
GPS waypoint or NDB
The receiver shows arrival at the active waypoint [[23:271|IFH 9-28]]
ADF alone: passage when the needle points to a wingtip or settles near 180°; it takes a few seconds at low altitude [[23:248|IFH 9-5]]

body.p: **A false passage.** On VOR receivers without an ON/OFF flag, transmitting on the combined NAV/COM can cause the same TO/FROM fluctuations as station passage. Read the whole receiver (TO/FROM, CDI and OBS) before deciding, and ignore readings taken while transmitting [[23:259|IFH 9-16]].

**Prompt entry.** Application: teach a fixed order at passage: turn to the entry heading, note the time, then report. The turn comes first [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8g]]; the time noted is the entry time ATC wants [[23:303|IFH 10-12]]; the report is time and altitude [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8f]].

callout.text: Application: in the briefing, have the learner say what passage will look like ("TO goes to FROM", "DME reads 15", "waypoint arrives") and the first heading to fly. If the answer is slow on the ground, the turn will be late in the airplane.

check.q: Approaching the VOR, your learner keys the mic for a call and the TO/FROM flickers. She starts the entry turn. What happened, and what do you teach?
check.a: On some receivers, transmitting causes TO/FROM fluctuations that look like station passage; read the whole receiver and never use a reading taken while transmitting [[23:259|IFH 9-16]]. Passage is the first complete reversal [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8g]].

chunks.title: Choosing the entry, and teaching the choice simply

body.p: The FAA recommends three entries, and the size and shape of the protected airspace were derived from them [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3(d)]]. The entry is chosen from the airplane's heading on arrival at the fix, and ±5° of heading is within good operating limits [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(d)]].

head: Entry
Sector
What the airplane does
rows: Parallel
Turn to parallel the holding course outbound on the nonholding side for one minute, turn back through more than 180°, and return to the fix or intercept the inbound course [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3(a)]]
Teardrop
Fly to the fix, turn outbound to a heading 30° into the holding side for one minute, then turn in the direction of the pattern to intercept the inbound course [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3(b)]]
Direct
Fly to the fix and turn to follow the pattern [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3(c)]]

body.p: Left-turn holds use the same entries, oriented to the 70° line on the holding side [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3(e)]]. An uncharted clearance states the turn direction only for left turns, on request, or when the controller thinks it necessary [[33:383|AIM 5-3-8i]], so no turns stated means right turns [[29:111|IPH 2-51]].

**A simple way to teach the choice.** Application: the angles in FIG 5-3-4 (a 70° teardrop sector and a 110° parallel sector) become one rule the learner can check on the heading indicator or HSI. Find the outbound course on the card, compared with the heading at the fix:

bullets: Right turns: outbound course 0 to 70° to the right of the heading means teardrop; 0 to 110° to the left means parallel; anything else means direct [[33:386|AIM FIG 5-3-4]].
Left turns: the mirror image. Outbound course within 70° to the left means teardrop; within 110° to the right means parallel; anything else means direct [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3(e)]].
Close to a boundary, either entry is acceptable, since ±5° is within limits [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(d)]].

body.p: Worked example: "Hold north of the VOR on the 360 radial," right turns. The inbound course is 180°, the outbound course 360°, and the holding side west. Arriving on 090°, the outbound course is 90° to the left: parallel. Arriving on 310°, it is 50° to the right: teardrop, flying 330° (30° into the holding side) for one minute. Arriving on 200°, it is 160° away: direct [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3]] [[23:303|IFH Figure 10-6]].

Build it in steps: draw the hold and its 70° line on paper for several clearances, then call the entry from the HSI on the ground, then fly it. Going from simple to complex keeps the learner from being overwhelmed [[25:177|AIH 9-7]], and having the learner visualize the flight first fits scenario training [[25:183|AIH 9-13]]. The IFH also suggests studying the compass rose and a quick reciprocal: for a heading over 180°, subtract 200 and add 20 [[23:186|IFH 7-25]].

callout.text: The AIM text says the parallel entry turns "in the direction of the holding pattern through more than 180 degrees" [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3(a)]]. Learners often read that as a right turn in a standard hold, but FIG 5-3-4 shows the return turn going back toward the holding side. Teach from the figure, and have the learner say which way the turn goes before reaching the fix.

check.q: "Hold southeast of the VOR on the 135 radial, left turns." Your learner arrives heading 100°. Using the heading rule, which entry?
check.a: Parallel. With left turns, an outbound course 0 to 110° to the right of the heading means parallel, and 135° is 35° to the right of 100°. This matches the mirrored sectors of FIG 5-3-4 [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3(e)]] [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3(a)]].

chunks.title: Timing: when the clock starts and how long the legs are

body.p: **Timing procedure.**

head: Item
Rule
rows: Inbound leg
1 minute at or below 14,000 ft MSL; 1½ minutes above [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4(a)]]
First outbound leg
1 or 1½ minutes by altitude; later outbound legs are adjusted to give the right inbound time [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4]]
Start of outbound timing
Over or abeam the fix, whichever is later; if abeam can't be found, when the turn outbound is complete [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4(b)]]
Entry time reported
The first arrival over the fix [[23:303|IFH 10-12]]
Parallel and teardrop entry legs
Checking the inbound time
Any navigation means available, such as DME or RNAV [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4]]

body.p: IFH Figure 10-7 shows how to find abeam at three kinds of fix [[23:303|IFH Figure 10-7]]:

bullets: VOR: timing starts when the TO/FROM indicator reverses on the outbound leg. That is the second reversal of the circuit; the first, over the station, starts the turn outbound [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8g]] [[23:303|IFH Figure 10-7]].
Airway intersection: the bearing that marks abeam can't be determined, so timing starts when the turn to outbound is complete [[23:303|IFH Figure 10-7]].
Compass locator: timing starts when the ADF relative bearing is 90° minus the drift correction angle [[23:303|IFH Figure 10-7]].

body.p: **Hold in lieu of procedure turn.** Fly it as depicted and do not exceed the charted leg length or time; maximum holding speeds still apply. If cleared for the approach before returning to the fix and at the right altitude, more circuits are not expected, and a pilot who wants them tells ATC [[33:428|AIM 5-4-9a5]].

callout.text: Two flips at a VOR hold: the flip over the station says turn; the flip abeam on the outbound leg says start the clock [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8g]] [[23:303|IFH Figure 10-7]].

check.q: Holding at a VOR, your learner starts the clock as she rolls out outbound, before the TO/FROM flips. What do you say?
check.a: Outbound timing starts over or abeam the fix, whichever is later [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4(b)]]; at a VOR, abeam is the TO/FROM reversal on the outbound leg [[23:303|IFH Figure 10-7]]. Starting early shortens the outbound leg. Only when abeam can't be found does timing start at the end of the outbound turn.

body.p: **Correction for wind drift.** A symmetrical racetrack can't be flown in wind. The pilot compensates for a known wind except when turning and adjusts outbound timing to get a 1-minute inbound leg (1½ minutes above 14,000 ft). Wind is countered with drift corrections on both legs and a time allowance on the outbound leg [[23:301|IFH 10-10]].
The sources' method, in the order you teach it:

bullets: 1. Find the inbound drift correction. When the CDI moves off center, correct toward it, starting with 20°; when the needle comes back to center, cut the correction in half, then refine [[23:257|IFH 9-14]]. Bracketing keeps the learner from chasing the needle, a listed VOR error [[23:259|IFH 9-16]].
2. Outbound, triple it the other way: correcting 8° left inbound means 24° right outbound. The AIM's reason is to avoid major turning adjustments [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(c)]].
3. Fly the turns at 3° per second or 30° of bank (25° with a flight director), whichever needs less bank, with no wind correction in them [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(b)]] [[23:301|IFH 10-10]].

4. Time the inbound leg and change the next outbound leg until the inbound leg is right: a long inbound leg calls for a shorter outbound leg, a short one for a longer outbound leg [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4]] [[23:301|IFH 10-10]].

body.p: Worked example: inbound course 040°. Your learner needs 046° to track it, 6° right, so the wind is from the right of the inbound course. Outbound on 220°, she corrects 18° the other way: 220° - 18° = 202° [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(c)]].
No source gives a number of seconds to change the outbound leg for each second of inbound error. Teach small changes and re-timing every inbound leg.

callout.text: Application: the first inbound leg is the wind finder. Have the learner say the correction as soon as the needle settles ("6 right inbound, so 18 left outbound") and bug the outbound heading before the fix. If the needle is still moving, the number is not ready.

check.q: Inbound course 300°; your learner tracks it with 294°. She plans 294° - 180° = 114° outbound. What is wrong, and what heading is right?
check.a: The reciprocal of the inbound heading puts the correction on the wrong side and does not triple it. Inbound she corrects 6° left, so outbound she corrects 18° right: 120° + 18° = 138° [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(c)]].

chunks.title: Use of DME in a holding pattern

body.p: **Use of DME in a holding pattern.** DME and GPS holds use the same entries and procedures, with distances in nautical miles in place of time. ATC or the approach chart gives the outbound leg length, and the DME or along-track distance readout marks its end [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j5]] [[23:304|IFH 10-13]]. On conventional holds both ends are measured from the DME station [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j5]].

head: Inbound leg
Outbound leg ends at
AIM example
rows: Toward the NAVAID
Fix distance plus leg length
10 NM fix, 5 NM legs: 15 DME [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j5]]
Away from the NAVAID
Fix distance minus leg length
28 NM fix, 8 NM legs: 20 DME [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j5]]

bullets: **Slant range.** DME reads slant range, not horizontal distance [[33:72|AIM 1-1-7b]]. The error is negligible at 1 NM or more from the facility for each 1,000 ft above it [[23:262|IFH 9-19]]. GPS distance used in place of DME puts the pattern slightly farther from the NAVAID; used only as a DME substitute, the difference is negligible and needs no action [[33:388|AIM 5-3-8j6]].

**DME checks a timed hold.** DME, RNAV or any other means may be used to get the right inbound time [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4]]. DME groundspeed is accurate only when tracking directly to or from the station [[23:260|IFH 9-17]], as on the inbound leg of a hold on a radial of that station.
**Which station?** A DME left in HOLD stays on the station it was tuned to before [[23:260|IFH 9-17]], so check that it reads from the holding facility.
**FMS differences.** Some FMS cue the inbound turn so the inbound leg matches the charted leg length; in high winds that enlarges the pattern, so crews must know their system [[29:134|IPH 3-22]].

callout.text: Application: before each DME hold, have the learner sketch a line with the NAVAID, the fix and the turn point and say "toward, so add" or "away, so subtract", using the AIM figures as the model [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j5]].

check.q: "Hold southwest of the 14 DME fix on the 230 radial, 4 mile legs." Where does the outbound leg end?
check.a: The pattern lies beyond the fix, away from the station, so the inbound leg runs toward the NAVAID: 14 + 4 = 18 DME [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j5]].

chunks.title: ATC reports and complying with the clearance

body.p: **Compliance with ATC reporting requirements.** Report the time and altitude when reaching the clearance limit, and report leaving it [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8f]]. Both are on the AIM list of reports made without an ATC request [[33:377|AIM 5-3-3]].

head: Situation
Report or rule
rows: Reaching a holding fix
"Marathon 564, FARGO Intersection at 05, 10,000, holding east." [[29:105|IPH Figure 2-68]]
Leaving a holding fix
"Marathon 564, leaving FARGO Intersection." [[29:105|IPH Figure 2-68]]
Unable to hold at the maximum speed
Tell ATC immediately and ask for another clearance [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(a)(2)]]
RNAV bank limit under 25° needed
Tell ATC that more holding area is needed [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(b)(4)]]
RNAV outbound leg getting too long
Notify ATC [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(f)]]
Navigation or radio malfunction
Report it as soon as practical with aircraft ID, equipment, how IFR capability is affected and the help wanted [[60:483|14 CFR 91.187(a)]] [[60:483|14 CFR 91.187(b)]]
Weather drops below the pilot's minimums
Tell ATC, which then issues instructions to keep holding or go to another airport [[23:302|IFH 10-11]]
Unforecast weather
Report it as soon as possible [[60:482|14 CFR 91.183(b)]]

body.p: Complying with the clearance: a pilot may not deviate from a clearance without an amended clearance, an emergency or a TCAS resolution advisory, and must ask at once when uncertain [[60:450|14 CFR 91.123(a)]]. "Roger" only means ATC received the call, not that it understood [[29:111|IPH 2-51]]. Keep the last assigned altitude unless the holding clearance gives a new one, and fly right turns unless left turns are assigned [[29:111|IPH 2-51]].

Leaving on time: when given a time to leave the fix, adjust the path inside the pattern to leave at that exact time [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8k]], and plan the last lap to leave as close as possible to the EFC [[29:111|IPH 2-51]]. ATC must know when an airplane leaves the fix before it can clear the next one into that airspace [[23:304|IFH 10-13]]. ATC also issues new instructions when a delay will exceed 1 hour or a revised EFC is needed [[23:302|IFH 10-11]].

callout.text: Two-way radio failure in IFR conditions: if the clearance limit is a fix where an approach begins, start the descent or approach as close as possible to the EFC; if not, leave at the EFC, go to a fix where an approach begins and start the approach as close as possible to the ETA [[60:483|14 CFR 91.185(c)(3)]]. That is why every holding clearance should include an EFC [[29:111|IPH 2-51]].

check.q: Your learner enters the hold well but says nothing to ATC. Afterward she says, "They have me on radar anyway." What do you teach?
check.a: Time and altitude on reaching the holding fix, and leaving it, are reports made without an ATC request [[33:377|AIM 5-3-3]] [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8f]]. Radar watch of holding airspace depends on workload and equipment and does not relieve the pilot of following the clearance [[33:392|AIM 5-3-8l]].

chunks.title: Using the MFD and moving map to monitor the hold

body.p: **Use of the MFD and other graphical navigational displays.** A moving map shows the airplane in relation to NAVAIDs, waypoints, airspace and terrain, which improves situational awareness [[23:29|IFH 1-10]]. An MFD can also show approach charts, terrain and weather [[23:123|IFH 5-28]]. Put the moving map in the scan; a smaller inset map on the PFD keeps the scan more centralized [[23:159|IFH 6-26]].

bullets: **What the map cannot tell you.** RNAV systems can't warn of leaving the holding protected airspace, because its dimensions are not in the database [[33:390|AIM 5-3-8j7(b)]].

**Where the RNAV turn point goes.** RNAV systems treat the leg distance as a maximum inbound leg, so the computed turn point is often beyond the design point, and with a strong headwind outbound it may reach or pass the edge of protected airspace [[33:389|AIM 5-3-8j7(a)(4)]]. Be ready to step in if the inbound turn does not begin near the charted leg length [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(f)]].

**Choose the automation level.** When an approach clearance is cancelled and a hold is coming, the RMH suggests basic autopilot modes such as heading and altitude while the pilot programs the change. Automation can also breed complacency and erode manual skill [[30:51|RMH 7-2]].

body.p: Teaching it, Application: for the first holds, declutter or cover the map so the learner builds the picture from the needles, the TO/FROM and the clock; then show the map and compare. Later, use the map from the start and ask the learner to predict the track before each turn. When the map and the needles disagree, teach her to reassess and get more information from the navigation instruments or ATC [[23:337|IFH 11-12]].

callout.text: ATC usually watches holding airspace on radar, but workload, traffic, weather and equipment can prevent it, and it never relieves the pilot of staying in the assigned hold [[33:392|AIM 5-3-8l]].

check.q: Your learner says the GPS map will warn him if the wind blows him out of the protected airspace. Is he right?
check.a: No. RNAV systems can't alert the pilot to excursions outside holding protected airspace, because its dimensions are not in the navigation database [[33:390|AIM 5-3-8j7(b)]].

chunks.title: Common errors: equipment, altitude, airspeed and bank

body.p: No FAA handbook in this course gives one list of holding errors, so this chunk and the next pair each PTS error with what the sources say causes it: what you see, the usual cause, and the fix you teach.
**Incorrect setting of aircraft navigation equipment.**

head: What you see
Usual cause
Fix and how to teach it
rows: The needle works, but the hold is in the wrong place
Careless tuning and identification [[23:257|IFH 9-14]]
Identify by code or decoded ID every time [[33:68|AIM 1-1-3c]]; make it part of the spoken setup
Corrections go the wrong way on a plain CDI
OBS on the reciprocal, or TO/FROM not checked after a course reversal [[23:257|IFH 9-14]]
Set the inbound course and expect reverse sensing outbound: turn away from the needle [[23:257|IFH 9-14]]. Show it on the ground by turning the OBS
GPS flies the wrong turns, or 1½-minute legs below 14,000 ft
Stored hold not checked, or limits taken from the wrong altitude [[33:390|AIM 5-3-8j7(c)(1)]] [[33:389|AIM 5-3-8j7(a)(5)]]
Check turns, speed, timing and distance against the clearance before the fix [[33:390|AIM 5-3-8j7(c)(1)]]
GPS moves on to the next waypoint after the fix
Sequencing not suspended [[23:273|IFH 9-30]]
Use the receiver's nonsequencing mode as the POH/AFM describes [[23:271|IFH 9-28]]
DME distance doesn't fit the chart
DME left in HOLD on another station [[23:260|IFH 9-17]]
Check the DME ID and source during setup [[23:260|IFH 9-17]]

body.p: **Inappropriate altitude, airspeed, and bank control.**

head: What you see
Usual cause
Fix and how to teach it
rows: Fast at the fix, pattern stretched
Slowing started late [[33:390|AIM 5-3-8j8(a)]]

At or below the maximum at least 3 minutes before the fix [[33:390|AIM 5-3-8j8(a)]]; excess speed with a poor entry can leave protected airspace [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3]]. Drill the racetrack pattern [[23:191|IFH 7-30]]
Altitude lost in each entry turn and gained on roll-out
Pitch not adjusted for the change in vertical lift [[23:186|IFH 7-25]]
Check pitch as bank pressure begins, and trim [[23:186|IFH 7-25]]
Bank too steep or wandering in the turns
Overcontrolling; bank not matched to standard rate [[23:186|IFH 7-25]]
Standard rate or 30°, whichever needs less bank [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(b)]]; start near airspeed / 10 + 7 [[23:88|IFH 4-11]]
Autopilot hold wide and long
Bank limit under 25° selected [[33:389|AIM 5-3-8j7(a)(3)]]
Select at least 25° unless limitations say otherwise; tell ATC if less is needed [[33:389|AIM 5-3-8j7(a)(3)]] [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(b)(4)]]
Airspeed and power erratic while slowing
Chasing the airspeed; abrupt pitch and bank changes [[23:187|IFH 7-26]]
Set holding power early, trim, and recheck the airspeed after each power change [[23:187|IFH 7-26]]

check.q: In every entry turn your learner loses about 80 ft, then climbs above altitude as she rolls out. Name the error and its cause.
check.a: Inappropriate altitude control in the turns. The IFH cause is failing to adjust pitch for the change in vertical lift, so altitude is lost on entry and gained on roll-out [[23:186|IFH 7-25]]. Have her check pitch as she starts the bank, and trim.

chunks.title: Common errors: timing, wind, fix passage and ATC

body.p: **Improper timing.**

head: What you see
Usual cause
Fix and how to teach it
rows: Outbound leg short, inbound leg long
Clock started before abeam [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4(b)]]
Over or abeam, whichever is later; at a VOR, wait for the TO/FROM to flip [[23:303|IFH Figure 10-7]]
Every outbound leg exactly 1 minute in a strong wind
Outbound time never adjusted [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4]]
Time each inbound leg and change the next outbound leg [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4]]
No time noted at the fix
Busy with the turn
The entry time is the first arrival over the fix [[23:303|IFH 10-12]]; teach turn, time, then talk

body.p: **Improper wind drift correction.**

head: What you see
Usual cause
Fix and how to teach it
rows: Inbound turn rolls out off course on the same side every lap
Outbound correction not tripled [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(c)]]
Triple the inbound correction, the other way [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(c)]]
Bank changed in the turns to fight the wind
Correcting while turning [[23:301|IFH 10-10]]
Correct on the legs only and keep the turns at standard rate [[23:301|IFH 10-10]] [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(b)]]
Heading chases the needle on the inbound leg
Homing, with corrections not bracketed [[23:259|IFH 9-16]]
Bracket: start with 20°, then halve it [[23:257|IFH 9-14]]

body.p: **Failure to recognize holding fix passage.**

head: What you see
Usual cause
Fix and how to teach it
rows: Turn starts late; the pattern drifts away from the fix
Waiting for the needle to settle, or misreading passage [[23:259|IFH 9-16]]
The first complete TO/FROM reversal means turn [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8g]]; read the whole receiver [[23:259|IFH 9-16]]
GPS starts the entry turn well before the fix
Fly-by turn on entry [[33:388|AIM 5-3-8j7(a)(2)]]
Slow at least 3 minutes out and use a 25° bank to limit it [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(e)]]

body.p: **Failure to comply with ATC instructions.**

head: What you see
Usual cause
Fix and how to teach it
rows: Holds on the wrong side or with the wrong turns
Clearance not understood; "roger" instead of a question [[29:111|IPH 2-51]]
Ask when uncertain [[60:450|14 CFR 91.123(a)]]; no turns stated means right turns [[33:383|AIM 5-3-8i]]
Leaves the fix early or late
Last lap not planned [[29:111|IPH 2-51]]
Adjust the pattern to leave at the time given [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8k]]
Exceeds a charted speed or leg limit
Chart limit missed [[33:385|AIM 5-3-8j2(b)]]
Brief the chart's limits; a hold in lieu of procedure turn must not exceed its charted leg [[33:428|AIM 5-4-9a5]]

check.q: On a windy day your learner's inbound turn rolls out left of course every lap. She uses the same 5° correction outbound as inbound. Name the error and the fix.
check.a: Improper wind drift correction: outbound she should triple the inbound correction and apply it the other way [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(c)]], and make the correction on the legs, not in the turns [[23:301|IFH 10-10]].

chunks.title: Demonstrate and explain: a right-seat talk-through

body.p: The PTS wants a demonstration flown to the instrument pilot skill level with an explanation that is clear, concise, technically accurate and complete, with no prompting [[FAA-S-8081-9E:15|PTS Unsatisfactory Performance]]. This is the first step of telling and doing: the demonstration should match the explanation and come in the same order, and any deviation should be acknowledged and explained at once [[25:177|AIH 9-7]]. Brief the positive exchange of flight controls before flight and use the three-step exchange [[25:178|AIH 9-8]] [[25:179|AIH 9-9]].
Sample talk-through for "Hold north of the VOR on the 360 radial, maintain 4,000, expect further clearance 1530," arriving on a heading of 090°:

bullets: "No turn direction was given, so right turns. Inbound course 180, outbound 360, holding side west [[33:383|AIM 5-3-8i]]."
"Setup: VOR tuned and identified, course set to 180, heading bug on 360, timer ready [[33:68|AIM 1-1-3c]] [[23:257|IFH 9-14]]."
"Entry: the outbound course is 90° to my left in a right-turn hold, so parallel [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3(a)]]."
"We have advance notice, so I'm at holding speed and power 3 minutes before the VOR [[33:390|AIM 5-3-8j8(a)]]."
"TO/FROM has fully reversed: station passage. Turning left to 360 to parallel outbound on the east side. Time noted [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8g]] [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3(a)]]."
"Report: VOR at 42, 4,000, holding north [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8f]] [[29:105|IPH Figure 2-68]]."
"One minute. Turning left, back toward the holding side, through more than 180° to intercept 180 inbound [[33:386|AIM FIG 5-3-4]]."
"Inbound I find my drift correction; outbound I'll triple it, the other way. Turns stay at standard rate [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(c)]] [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(b)]]."
"Over the VOR I turn right to 360. When the TO/FROM flips abeam, I start one minute [[23:303|IFH Figure 10-7]]."
"I time the inbound leg and adjust the next outbound leg to make it one minute [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4]]."

body.p: Then move through the rest of telling and doing: the learner tells while you fly, which shows you whether she understands before she is busy flying, and then the learner tells and flies [[25:178|AIH 9-8]].

callout.text: Application: keep the words short at the fix (turn, time, talk) and save the why for the outbound leg, when the workload is lower. The PTS also expects a realistic distraction during the flight [[FAA-S-8081-9E:16|PTS Use of Distractions]], so practice the talk-through with a radio call thrown in.

check.q: During your demonstration you forget to start the clock abeam the VOR and notice it 15 seconds later. What do you do?
check.a: Say so at once and explain it. When a demonstration does not match the explanation, the deviation should be acknowledged and explained immediately [[25:177|AIH 9-7]].

chunks.title: Analyze and correct: when the evaluator flies the errors

body.p: During the flight, the evaluator acts as a student in selected maneuvers to see whether you can analyze and correct simulated common errors, and describing, recognizing, analyzing and correcting those errors is one of the PTS's satisfactory-performance items [[FAA-S-8081-9E:14|PTS Evaluator Responsibility]] [[FAA-S-8081-9E:15|PTS Satisfactory Performance]]. Expect a wrong entry, a clock started at the fix, an outbound heading with no wind correction, or a missed report.
Application: a four-step routine for the right seat:

head: Step
What you do
rows: Notice
Watch the needles and the clock, not only the airplane, and say what you see: "We're 20 seconds outbound and the TO/FROM hasn't flipped."
Name it
Use the PTS words, such as "improper timing" or "improper wind drift correction".
Find the cause
Ask the learner why it happened before you explain; it tells you whether it was a slip or a mistake [[25:84|AIH 3-33]] [[25:86|AIH 3-35]]
Fix and replay
Give the source rule, then have the learner fly the next lap correctly; reteach by demonstrating, practicing under direction and observing [[25:181|AIH 9-11]]

body.p: Slip or mistake? A slip is an error of action, such as forgetting the clock; a mistake is an error of thought, such as believing the outbound correction equals the inbound one [[25:84|AIH 3-33]]. Some errors simply show a need for more practice; others point to methods or habits that need to change [[25:85|AIH 3-34]].

Safety permitting, let the learner go part of the way into an error and find the way out; a learner who seldom corrects an error learns poorly. To test real understanding, vary the task, for example left turns instead of right or a DME hold instead of a timed one [[25:182|AIH 9-12]]. In a hold, the limit is the protected airspace: a poor entry flown too fast can leave it [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3]], so stop the error before that.

callout.text: Under the PTS, any action or lack of action that makes the evaluator step in to keep the flight safe is a reason for failure, and so is poor visual scanning to clear the area [[FAA-S-8081-9E:15|PTS Unsatisfactory Performance]]. Teaching the error never replaces flying and watching outside.

check.q: The evaluator, playing your student, flies the outbound leg on the reciprocal of his inbound heading in a strong crosswind. What do you say?
check.a: Name it (improper wind drift correction), explain that the reciprocal puts the correction on the wrong side and does not triple it, and give the fix: triple the inbound correction, the other way [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(c)]]. Then have him fly the next outbound leg correctly [[25:181|AIH 9-11]].

The shaded slice at the upper left is sector (a), the 70 degree slice at the lower left is sector (b), and the rest of the circle on both sides of the tilted line is marked (c). Dashed lines show the parallel entry (outbound below the line, then a turn back up toward the holding side) and the teardrop entry. The words No Wind appear at the lower right.

Bottom: a hold at a compass locator with a 330 degree bearing line; the caption reads outbound timing starts when ADF relative bearing is 90 degrees minus drift correction angle.

scenario.title: Left turns at Kenton VOR in a strong west wind
scenario.setup: You are a CFII flying with Maya, an instrument learner with about 30 hours of instrument time, in a Piper Archer. NAV 1 drives an HSI and can be switched between an IFR-approved GPS navigator and its VOR receiver; NAV 2 is a VOR with a plain CDI. There is no DME. She is under a view-limiting device in VMC and you are also the safety pilot. The wind at 4,000 ft is from 270° at 30 knots. Approach says: "Archer 4MK, hold northeast of the Kenton VOR on the 045 radial, left turns, maintain 4,000, expect further clearance 1530." She is flying direct to the VOR on a heading of 090°.

questions.q: Before she reaches the VOR, what setup do you expect to hear from her?
questions.a: Tune and identify the VOR [[33:68|AIM 1-1-3c]], set the inbound course of 225° [[23:257|IFH 9-14]], bug the first heading [[25:85|AIH 3-34]] and ready the timer. If she uses the GPS, she checks that its hold has left turns and the right leg and speed [[33:390|AIM 5-3-8j7(c)(1)]]; some systems store holds as standard and need pilot action for left turns [[33:390|AIM 5-3-8j7(c)]].

questions.q: Which entry should she fly, and what heading after the VOR?
questions.a: The outbound course, 045°, is 45° to the left of her 090° heading; in a left-turn hold that is the teardrop sector, oriented to the 70° line just as in a standard hold [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3(e)]]. The holding side is southeast, so she flies 30° from the outbound course into that side, 075°, for one minute, then turns left to intercept 225° inbound [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3(b)]].

questions.q: With the wind from 270°, she needs 233° to track 225° inbound. What outbound heading should she plan, and what do you watch in the first circuit?
questions.a: 8° right inbound means 24° left outbound: 045° - 24° = 021° [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(c)]]. Watch that she corrects on the legs, not in the turns [[23:301|IFH 10-10]], starts the clock when the TO/FROM flips abeam [[23:303|IFH Figure 10-7]] and times the inbound leg [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4]].

questions.q: Her first inbound leg takes 1 minute 25 seconds. What do you teach?
questions.a: The outbound leg was too long for this wind, with a tailwind outbound and a headwind inbound. Shorten the next outbound leg to bring the inbound leg to 1 minute [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4]] [[23:301|IFH 10-10]]. No source gives a seconds formula, so adjust and re-time each lap.

questions.q: To give her a setup error to find, you set NAV 2's OBS to 045° while she is busy. On the next inbound leg she cross-checks NAV 2 and starts correcting the wrong way. How do you handle it?
questions.a: Safety permitting, let her go part of the way into the error and find the way out [[25:182|AIH 9-12]]. Then have her name the cause: with the OBS on the reciprocal, the CDI senses in reverse, and not checking the TO/FROM is a listed VOR error [[23:257|IFH 9-14]]. Ask her why it happened before you explain [[25:86|AIH 3-35]], reset 225° and fly the next lap.

questions.q: At 1525 she has said nothing to ATC since the VOR and asks what she would do if the radio failed now in IMC.
questions.a: She should have reported time and altitude at the VOR, and she must report leaving it [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8f]] [[33:377|AIM 5-3-3]]. With lost radios in IFR conditions: if Kenton is where her approach begins, she starts the approach as close as possible to 1530; if not, she leaves at 1530 for a fix where an approach begins and starts it as close as possible to her ETA [[60:483|14 CFR 91.185(c)(3)]].

skills.do: From the right seat, fly a hold to the instrument pilot standard while explaining the clearance, the equipment setup, the entry choice, fix passage, timing, wind correction and the reports, in the same order you fly them.
skills.practice: Fly the talk-through for a VOR hold, a DME hold and a GPS hold in a simulator or with a safety pilot, explaining in the order you fly [[25:177|AIH 9-7]]. Warm up with the IFH racetrack pattern to set the timing and speed habits [[23:191|IFH 7-30]].

skills.do: When the evaluator, as your student, makes holding errors, notice each one, name it in the PTS words, find the cause, give the fix and have the student fly it again.
skills.practice: Have another applicant fly holds with planted errors (wrong entry, early clock, untripled correction, missed report, wrong DME source) and run the notice, name, cause, fix routine. Ask the learner why before you tell [[25:86|AIH 3-35]].

quiz.q: Your learner asks why she must identify the holding VOR when its needle is already centered. What is the only positive way to identify a VOR?
options: Its Morse code or recorded voice ID
The FSS voice heard on that frequency
A centered needle with a TO indication
A frequency that matches the chart
quiz.why: Only the Morse code or the recorded voice identification positively identifies a VOR [[33:68|AIM 1-1-3c]]. FSS voice transmissions are not reliable for this, because one FSS may run several VORs with other names [[33:69|AIM 1-1-3c]].

quiz.q: Your learner holds at an airway intersection at 5,000 ft and can't tell when she is abeam the fix. When does she start the outbound clock?
options: When the inbound turn begins at the far end
The moment she crosses the fix inbound
When the turn to outbound is fully completed
After flying one minute past the fix
quiz.why: If the abeam position can't be determined, timing starts when the turn to outbound is completed [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4(b)]], as IFH Figure 10-7 shows for an intersection [[23:303|IFH Figure 10-7]]. Starting at the fix itself would shorten the outbound leg.

quiz.q: Inbound course 090°. Your learner holds 097° to track it. What outbound heading do you expect her to fly?
quiz.why: She corrects 7° right inbound, so outbound she triples it the other way: 270° - 21° = 249° [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(c)]]. 291° applies the triple correction on the wrong side; 263° is not tripled.

quiz.q: In a standard (right-turn) hold, your learner arrives at the fix with the outbound course 40° to the right of her heading. Which entry fits the FIG 5-3-4 sectors?
options: Direct
Parallel
Teardrop
Either parallel or direct
quiz.why: By the heading rule drawn from FIG 5-3-4, an outbound course 0 to 70° to the right of the heading in a right-turn hold falls in sector (b), the teardrop [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3(b)]]. 40° is far from a boundary, so the ±5° allowance does not make another entry acceptable [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(d)]].

quiz.q: ATC gave your learner advance notice of a hold. By when does the AIM recommend she be at or below the maximum holding speed?
options: When first crossing the holding fix
At least 3 minutes before crossing the fix
Within 5 NM of the holding fix
By the end of her first outbound leg in the hold
quiz.why: With advance notice, start slowing to be at or below the maximum at least 3 minutes before crossing the fix [[33:390|AIM 5-3-8j8(a)]]. Crossing the fix at that speed is the minimum when there is no clearance beyond it [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8d]].

quiz.q: "Hold northeast of the 12 DME fix on the 045 radial, 5 mile legs." At what DME reading does your learner turn inbound?
options: 7 DME
12 DME
22 DME
17 DME
quiz.why: The pattern is beyond the fix, so the inbound leg runs toward the NAVAID and the outbound end is fix distance plus leg length: 12 + 5 = 17 DME [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j5]]. 7 DME would be right only if the inbound leg ran away from the NAVAID.

quiz.q: Why does the IFH say a holding speed reduction starts when 3 minutes or less from the fix?
options: To save fuel for the expected delay
To stay inside the holding airspace
To give ATC time to approve the entry
To let the gyros settle before the turn
quiz.why: The purpose is to keep from overshooting the holding airspace limits, especially where adjacent holds are close together [[23:302|IFH 10-11]]. Slowing early may also save time in the hold [[29:112|IPH 2-52]], but that is not the reason given.

quiz.q: On a plain CDI with the OBS set to the inbound course, what will your learner see on the outbound leg?
options: Reverse sensing, so she turns away from the needle
Normal sensing, so she turns toward the needle
An OFF flag until the TO/FROM indicator flips
A needle that stays centered until abeam
quiz.why: Outbound she flies the reciprocal of the selected course, which gives reverse sensing: turn away from the needle to correct [[23:257|IFH 9-14]]. An HSI instead pictures the airplane against the selected course as if seen from above [[23:118|IFH 5-23]].

quiz.q: Your learner's GPS has a hold stored at the clearance fix. What must she confirm before using it?
options: Only that the fix name matches the chart
That it will always choose a direct entry
Its turns, speed limit, timing and distance
That the hold appears on the moving map
quiz.why: Pilots using a database hold must confirm it matches the assigned hold in turn direction, speed limit, timing and distance [[33:390|AIM 5-3-8j7(c)(1)]]. Many systems choose the entry themselves, sometimes from ground track [[33:388|AIM 5-3-8j7(a)(1)]].

quiz.q: Your learner asks which holding reports the AIM expects without an ATC request. What do you answer?
options: The entry type and the outbound heading
Fuel remaining, then each inbound leg time
Only leaving it, since radar shows the arrival
Time and altitude there, then leaving it
quiz.why: Report the time and altitude on reaching a holding fix and when leaving it, at all times and without a request [[33:377|AIM 5-3-3]] [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8f]]. Radar does not remove the arrival report.

quiz.q: Your learner wants the GPS-coupled autopilot's 15° bank limit on in the hold to keep the turns gentle. What does the AIM say?
options: Fine, since a shallow bank keeps the hold tight
At least 25°, or tell ATC more room is needed
Fine below 14,000 ft with 1-minute legs
Fine, since GPS guidance corrects the track
quiz.why: Do not use bank limits under 25° unless required; if bank must be limited below 25°, tell ATC that more holding area is needed [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(b)(4)]]. A shallower bank makes the pattern wider and longer, not tighter [[33:389|AIM 5-3-8j7(a)(3)]].

quiz.q: In IFH Figure 10-7, holding at a compass locator, when does outbound timing start?
options: When the needle first points at the tail
At 90° relative, minus the drift correction
When the turn to outbound is fully complete
When the needle swings through 270° relative
quiz.why: The figure says outbound timing starts when the ADF relative bearing is 90° minus the drift correction angle [[23:303|IFH Figure 10-7]]. Timing at the end of the outbound turn is the intersection case, where abeam can't be found.

final_quiz.q: "Hold southwest of the VOR on the 225 radial," no turn direction given. Your learner arrives heading 090°. Which entry?
options: Direct
Parallel
Teardrop
Parallel or teardrop
final_quiz.why: No turns stated means right turns [[29:111|IPH 2-51]]. The outbound course, 225°, is 135° to the right of 090°: not within 70° right (teardrop) nor 110° left (parallel), so it is in the direct sector of FIG 5-3-4 [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3(c)]].

final_quiz.q: Same hold, southwest on the 225 radial with right turns. Your learner arrives heading 180°. What does she fly after the VOR?
options: Teardrop: about 255° for one minute
Parallel: 225° on the northwest side
Direct: turn right to 225°
Teardrop: about 195° for one minute
final_quiz.why: 225° is 45° to the right of 180°, the teardrop sector. The holding side is southeast, so the teardrop heading is 30° from the outbound course into that side: 195° for one minute [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3(b)]]. 255° would put the teardrop on the nonholding side.

final_quiz.q: At 6,000 ft your learner's inbound legs keep taking 45 seconds. What change do you teach?
options: Fly 1½-minute legs at this altitude
Lengthen the next outbound leg
Shorten the next outbound leg
Steepen the bank in the turns
final_quiz.why: Outbound timing is adjusted to achieve the proper inbound time, 1 minute at or below 14,000 ft [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4]]. A short inbound leg needs a longer outbound leg. Changing the bank is not the method; turns stay at standard rate or 30° [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(b)]].

final_quiz.q: Your learner flies VOR holds well, but you suspect she is copying a pattern without understanding it. What does the AIH suggest?
options: Vary it, such as left turns or a DME hold
Repeat the same hold until it is perfect
Move on, since her flying meets the standard
Give a written test before the next flight
final_quiz.why: When you suspect a learner performs correctly without understanding, require her to vary the maneuver, combine it with others or apply its elements elsewhere [[25:182|AIH 9-12]]. Repeating the same hold would not reveal the gap.

final_quiz.q: Holding at a VOR, your learner keys the mic and the TO/FROM flickers. She starts the outbound turn. Which IFH error is this?
options: Chasing the CDI instead of tracking
Careless tuning and identification
Misinterpreting station passage
Reverse sensing from the OBS setting
final_quiz.why: Misinterpretation of station passage: transmitting can cause the same TO/FROM fluctuations as passage, so read the whole receiver and ignore readings taken while transmitting [[23:259|IFH 9-16]].

final_quiz.q: The evaluator, as your student, flies the holding turns at 35° of bank at 95 knots. What standard do you teach?
options: A 30° bank in every holding turn, every time
Whatever bank angle the autopilot happens to select
A gentle 15° bank so the hold stays small
Standard rate or 30°, whichever needs less bank
final_quiz.why: Make holding turns at 3° per second or 30° of bank (25° with a flight director), whichever needs the least bank [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(b)]]. At 95 knots standard rate needs about 16° to 17° by the IFH rule of thumb [[23:88|IFH 4-11]], so 30° every time is wrong.

final_quiz.q: Your learner uses GPS in place of an inoperative DME to fly a DME hold. What does the AIM say about the distance difference?
options: Negligible when used only to substitute
Add altitude in miles to each GPS reading
Not allowed; GPS can't replace DME in a hold
Fly timed legs to make up the difference
final_quiz.why: RNAV distance may replace DME when holding; the pattern sits slightly farther from the NAVAID, but used solely for DME substitution the difference is negligible and no pilot action is needed [[33:388|AIM 5-3-8j6]]. Holding over a DME fix with a suitable RNAV system is allowed [[33:117|AIM 1-2-3c]].

final_quiz.q: In FIG 5-3-9, why does the RNAV turn point fall well beyond the design turn point?
options: It ignores the published leg distance completely
It treats the leg length as the inbound leg
The pilot selected too steep a bank limit
Database holds always use 1½-minute legs
final_quiz.why: RNAV systems apply the leg distance as the maximum inbound leg and compute the outbound turn point from it; with a strong headwind outbound, that point moves farther out, possibly beyond protected airspace [[33:389|AIM 5-3-8j7(a)(4)]].

final_quiz.q: Your learner holds at a fix where her approach begins, with an EFC of 1450. The radio fails in IMC. When does she start the approach?
options: At the original flight plan ETA
Right away, once the radios fail
As close as possible to the 1450 EFC
After one more full holding circuit
final_quiz.why: When the clearance limit is a fix where an approach begins, start descent or the approach as close as possible to the EFC time [[60:483|14 CFR 91.185(c)(3)]]. The ETA is used only when no EFC was received.

final_quiz.q: ATC cancels your learner's approach clearance and says to expect holding. She is head-down reprogramming the GPS, autopilot in NAV mode. What does the RMH suggest?
options: Disconnect the autopilot and hand-fly while typing
Stay in NAV mode and finish typing quickly
Refuse the hold and ask ATC for vectors
Use heading and altitude modes while she programs
final_quiz.why: In this exact case the RMH suggests basic autopilot modes such as heading and altitude, so the pilot can program the change while the flight path stays under control [[30:51|RMH 7-2]]. Failing to move to a lower automation level is one of the most common errors [[30:51|RMH 7-2]].

final_quiz.q: With advance notice of holding and a groundspeed of 120 knots, at least how far from the fix should your learner be at or below the maximum holding speed?
options: 6 NM
3 NM
2 NM
12 NM
final_quiz.why: Be at or below the maximum at least 3 minutes before the fix [[33:390|AIM 5-3-8j8(a)]]. At 120 knots, 2 NM per minute x 3 minutes = 6 NM.

final_quiz.q: Which of these learner errors is a slip rather than a mistake?
options: Believing the outbound correction equals the inbound one
Forgetting to start the clock abeam the fix
Thinking a clearance with no turns means left turns
Thinking the parallel entry turns away from the holding side
final_quiz.why: A slip is an error of action, often simply neglecting to do something; a mistake is an error of thought, such as a misconception [[25:84|AIH 3-33]]. The other three are misconceptions.

final_quiz.q: ATC says the maximum holding airspeed is 175 knots. Your learner's twin needs 185 knots in the icing it is in. What should she do?
options: Hold at 185 knots and tell ATC after one lap
Hold at 175 even close to the stall warning
Tell ATC at once and request another clearance
Fly 185 knots but shorten the legs to fit
final_quiz.why: Advise ATC immediately if unable to comply with the maximum holding airspeed and request an alternate clearance; speeds above it can take the airplane outside protected airspace [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(a)(2)]].

final_quiz.q: In a VOR hold as shown in IFH Figure 10-7, what does the TO/FROM indicator do abeam the station on the outbound leg, and what does it mean?
options: It reverses; begin the turn inbound
It shows OFF; ignore the VOR until inbound
It stays steady; time from the fix instead
It reverses; start the outbound timing
final_quiz.why: At a VOR, outbound timing starts when the TO/FROM indicator reverses abeam the station [[23:303|IFH Figure 10-7]]. The earlier reversal over the station is the cue to begin the turn outbound [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8g]].

final_quiz.q: Your learner holds on a radial of a VOR/DME and wants to use DME groundspeed on the inbound leg to judge the wind. Is the reading useful there?
options: No; DME groundspeed is never usable in a hold
Only if the DME is in its HOLD mode at the time
Yes, when tracking to or from the station
Only when the airplane is above 14,000 feet MSL
final_quiz.why: DME groundspeed is accurate only when tracking directly to or from the station [[23:260|IFH 9-17]], as on an inbound leg along a radial. The DME HOLD function only keeps the DME on a station; it has nothing to do with groundspeed accuracy [[23:260|IFH 9-17]].

takeaways: Set up early: tune and identify, inbound course on the OBS or HSI, heading bug, timer, and check any GPS hold against the clearance.
Maximum speeds are 200, 230 and 265 KIAS by altitude unless charted lower; be at or below them 3 minutes before the fix.
At a VOR the flip over the station says turn; the flip abeam on the outbound leg says start the clock.
Teach the entry with one heading rule drawn from FIG 5-3-4, and allow ±5° near a line.
Wind: correct on the legs, triple the inbound correction outbound, and adjust the outbound time for a 1-minute inbound leg.
DME holds: inbound toward the NAVAID, add the leg length; away from it, subtract.
Report time and altitude at the fix and when leaving; ask when unsure; the EFC is the exit plan if the radio fails.
When the evaluator flies errors: notice, name it in PTS words, find the cause, give the fix, replay.
cfi_notes: This Task is on every CFII practical test unless you already hold an instrument instructor rating in another category [[FAA-S-8081-9E:18|PTS Additional Rating Table]]: the Area VII NOTE says the evaluator shall select Tasks A and B [[FAA-S-8081-9E:38|PTS Area VII NOTE]]. The evaluator also acts as a student in selected maneuvers, so expect simulated holding errors.

The IFH speed table says "up to 6,000 feet" and calls maximum holding airspeed "MHA" [[23:302|IFH 10-11]]; the AIM table starts at the MHA [[33:385|AIM 5-3-8j2(a)]], and the P/CG uses MHA for minimum holding altitude [[34:379|P/CG M-4]]. Teach the AIM terms.
The IFH lists "a bank angle provided by a flight director system" [[23:303|IFH 10-12]]; the current AIM gives 25° with a flight director, using whichever bank is least [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(b)]].

Speed-limit depiction: the IFH and IPH say a nonstandard holding speed is shown by an icon [[23:302|IFH 10-11]] [[29:112|IPH 2-52]]; the AIM describes that icon as the racetrack symbol with the speed in its center [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8h NOTE]] and gives the example (175) in parentheses inside the pattern [[33:385|AIM 5-3-8j2(b)]]. The sources agree; show learners the symbol on real charts.

Slowing rules differ in wording: start slowing when 3 minutes or less from the clearance limit [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8d]]; with advance notice be at or below the maximum at least 3 minutes before the fix [[33:390|AIM 5-3-8j8(a)]]; the IPH says ATC expects the pilot to slow to the limit within 3 minutes of the ETA [[29:112|IPH 2-52]]. With advance notice, teach the stricter j8(a).

The AIM and IFH both describe the parallel return turn as "in the direction of the holding pattern" [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3(a)]] [[23:303|IFH 10-12]], while FIG 5-3-4 shows it going back toward the holding side. Application: be ready to explain which way it turns, using the figure. The IFH also points readers to AIM 5-3-7 for entries; holding is now 5-3-8 [[23:303|IFH 10-12]].

The IFH gives two standard-rate bank rules of thumb: airspeed / 10 + 7 [[23:88|IFH 4-11]] and 15 percent of true airspeed [[23:212|IFH 7-51]]. At 90 knots they give 16° and about 13.5°. Either is a starting point; the turn rate indicator is the primary bank instrument in the turn [[23:212|IFH 7-51]].

The IFH presents GPS as a substitute for ADF and DME, such as holding over an NDB [[23:270|IFH 9-27]]; the current AIM also allows holding over a VOR or DME fix with a suitable RNAV system [[33:117|AIM 1-2-3c]]. Teach the AIM.

A useful oral question: cleared for the approach while established in a published hold above the published minimum holding altitude, the pilot may descend to that MHA [[33:392|AIM 5-3-8l4]]; where no MHA is published, keep the last assigned altitude until leaving the hold and established inbound [[33:392|AIM 5-3-8m]]. The Instrument lesson IR.III.B covers the pilot's side, including fuel planning after a new EFC.
gaps: No source gives a rule for how many seconds to change the outbound leg for each second of inbound-leg error.
Holding speed, power and fuel flow for the training airplane come from its POH/AFM, which is not in the sources.

The PTS lists the holding common errors [[FAA-S-8081-9E:39|PTS VII.B]]; no handbook gathers them in one place, so the error tables pair those PTS items with AIM cautions and the IFH's VOR, turn and power errors.
No source gives a rule of thumb for choosing the entry; the heading rule in this lesson is derived from the 70° and 110° sectors of FIG 5-3-4.
GPS and MFD holding pages and buttons differ by manufacturer, and the AIM says RNAV holding varies widely [[33:388|AIM 5-3-8j7]]; use the installed unit's pilot guide.

The Instrument Rating ACS holding standards: change to holding airspeed when 3 minutes or less from, but prior to arriving at, the fix [[FAA-S-ACS-8C:15|IR ACS IR.III.B.S2]]; airspeed ±10 knots, altitude ±100 feet, selected headings within ±10° and a course within ¾-scale CDI deflection [[FAA-S-ACS-8C:15|IR ACS IR.III.B.S4]]; see the Instrument lesson IR.III.B.

activities.title: Set up for a VOR hold
activities.intro: Tap a piece of equipment, then how you set it before the fix.

pairs.r: Tuned and identified by code or voice ID
On the holding facility, ID checked
Ready at the fix, restarted over or abeam
Turns, speed, timing and distance checked

activities.title: Arriving at a VOR hold
activities.intro: Use the arrows to put the steps in order, then tap Check.
steps: Read back the clearance and ask about anything unclear
Tune and identify the VOR and set the inbound course
Pick the entry from the heading at the fix and bug its heading
At least 3 minutes out, be at holding speed
At the first full TO/FROM reversal, turn to the entry heading
Note the time and report time and altitude
Fly the entry, then time outbound from over or abeam the fix

activities.title: Left turns: pick the entry
activities.intro: "Hold southeast of the VOR on the 135 radial, left turns." Inbound course 315°, outbound 135°, holding side southwest. Tap each arrival heading, then its entry.
activities.why: Left-turn entries are oriented to the 70° line on the holding side, the mirror of FIG 5-3-4 [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3(e)]]. With left turns, outbound course within 70° to the left of the heading is teardrop, within 110° to the right is parallel, and the rest is direct.

activities.title: Read the entry diagram
activities.intro: Drag each label to its numbered pin on AIM FIG 5-3-4.
activities.why: Sectors (a) parallel, (b) teardrop and (c) direct, divided by the 70° line through the fix [[33:386|AIM 5-3-8j3]] [[33:386|AIM FIG 5-3-4]].

activities.title: Hold math you will teach
activities.intro: Work it out, then type your answer.

items.q: Inbound course 220°. Your learner needs 226° to track it. What outbound heading should she fly? (Type 22 for 022°.)
Left-turn hold, inbound course 150°. Your learner tracks it with 144°. What outbound heading should she fly?
items.why: 6° left inbound, so 18° right outbound: 330° + 18° = 348°. Turn direction does not change the triple rule [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(c)]].

items.q: "Hold southwest of the 14 DME fix on the 230 radial, 4 mile legs." At what DME does the outbound leg end?
items.why: The pattern is beyond the fix, so the inbound leg is toward the NAVAID: 14 + 4 = 18 DME [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j5]].

items.q: "Hold southwest of the 22 DME fix on the 045 radial, 5 mile legs." At what DME does the outbound leg end?
items.why: The pattern lies between the fix and the station, so the inbound leg runs away from the NAVAID: 22 - 5 = 17 DME [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j5]].

items.q: With advance notice of holding and a groundspeed of 105 knots, at least how many NM before the fix should your learner be at holding speed?
items.why: At least 3 minutes before the fix [[33:390|AIM 5-3-8j8(a)]]: 105 / 60 = 1.75 NM per minute x 3 = 5.25 NM.

items.q: Holding 4,000 ft above a VORTAC, at least how far from it must the airplane be for DME slant-range error to be negligible?
items.why: Slant-range error is negligible at 1 NM or more from the facility for each 1,000 ft above it: 4 NM [[23:262|IFH 9-19]].

activities.title: Teaching the first holding lesson
activities.intro: You are teaching holds to Ben, an instrument learner, in a trainer with a six-pack, one VOR with a plain CDI, an IFR GPS and a timer. Today: a ground briefing, then VOR holds in VMC with Ben under the view-limiting device.

steps.s: Ground briefing. Ben has never flown a hold. Where do you start?
options: Brief all three entries, DME holds and GPS holds so the flight covers everything
Skip the briefing, since holds are learned best by flying them under the hood
Have Ben read AIM 5-3-8 on his own and quiz him on it after the flight
Start with the pattern, timing and turns, then add one entry, simple to complex
steps.why: Teaching several skills at once works best from simple to complex [[25:177|AIH 9-7]]. The IFH racetrack pattern builds the timing and turns before entries are added [[23:191|IFH 7-30]].

steps.s: In the air you demonstrate the first hold. While you fly, what do you do?
options: Fly it silently first, then explain everything afterward on the ground
Explain in the order you briefed, and say so if the demo strays
Let Ben fly the first one while you explain it from the right seat
Put it on the autopilot so Ben can watch the moving map instead
steps.why: In the first step of telling and doing, the demonstration follows the explanation in the same order, and any deviation is acknowledged and explained at once [[25:177|AIH 9-7]].

steps.s: Ben now flies. At the VOR he waits about 15 seconds for the needle to steady before turning.
options: Let it go, since a calm late turn beats a rushed early one
Take the controls and fly the turn yourself to show the timing
Teach that the first complete TO/FROM reversal is the cue to turn
Have him wait for the GPS to confirm passage before every turn
steps.why: Begin the turn outbound at the first complete reversal of the TO/FROM indicator [[33:382|AIM 5-3-8g]]; protected airspace assumes the airplane flies over the fix on entry [[33:388|AIM 5-3-8j7(a)(2)]], so a late turn costs room.

steps.s: Outbound, Ben starts the clock as he rolls out, before the TO/FROM flips.
options: Tell him timing starts over or abeam the fix, whichever is later
Let it go; starting the clock early only costs a few seconds
Tell him to start timing at the fix itself on every circuit
Tell him to skip timing outbound and time only the inbound leg
steps.why: Outbound timing begins over or abeam the fix, whichever occurs later [[33:387|AIM 5-3-8j4(b)]]; at a VOR, abeam is the TO/FROM reversal on the outbound leg [[23:303|IFH Figure 10-7]].

steps.s: Inbound he tracks with a 5° left correction. He bugs his outbound heading with 5° right.
options: Fine; the same correction, applied the other way
Triple it: 15° right of the outbound course
No correction outbound; fix it with timing alone
15° left of the outbound course instead
steps.why: When outbound, triple the inbound drift correction to avoid major turning adjustments: 5° left inbound means 15° right outbound [[33:391|AIM 5-3-8j8(c)]].

options: Hand him a grade sheet listing every error you saw
Ask him to assess himself first, then compare with yours
Tell him it all went fine to keep his morale up
Skip it, since you covered each error in flight
steps.why: Collaborative assessment starts with the learner's self-assessment, followed by a discussion comparing it with the instructor's assessment [[25:182|AIH 9-12]].

activities.title: True or false: equipment, maps and reports
activities.intro: Decide whether each statement is true or false.

cards.s: A DME with its HOLD function set stays on the station selected before HOLD was set.
cards.why: True [[23:260|IFH 9-17]]. Check the DME source before a DME hold.

cards.s: An RNAV system will alert the pilot when the airplane leaves holding protected airspace.
cards.why: False. Those dimensions are not in the navigation database, so RNAV systems can't alert for excursions [[33:390|AIM 5-3-8j7(b)]].

cards.s: If the reported weather drops below the pilot's minimums while holding, the pilot should tell ATC.
cards.why: True. ATC then issues instructions to continue holding or proceed to another airport [[23:302|IFH 10-11]].

cards.s: In radar contact, the time and altitude report on reaching a holding fix may be left out.
cards.why: False. It is listed under reports made at all times; the only exception is instrument training at military terminal facilities with radar service [[33:377|AIM 5-3-3]].

cards.s: In a parallel entry, the one-minute leg is flown on the nonholding side.
Cleared for the approach from a hold in lieu of procedure turn while at the right altitude, the pilot is expected to fly one more circuit.
cards.why: False. Additional circuits are not necessary nor expected; a pilot who wants them tells ATC [[33:428|AIM 5-4-9]].
